script: export const meta = { name: 'ydp-spec-verify', description: 'Verify every spec functional example and API signature against the implementation', phases: [ { title: 'Examples', detail: 'run each of the 19 spec functional examples' }, { title: 'Signatures', detail: 'verify class/function signatures and config defaults' }, { title: 'Gaps', detail: 'adversarial hunt for untested spec surface' }, ], } const RESULT = { type: 'object', properties: { label: { type: 'string' }, status: { type: 'string', enum: ['PASS', 'FAIL', 'PARTIAL'] }, detail: { type: 'string', description: 'What you ran and what happened. Include exact error text on failure.' }, fix_needed: { type: 'string', description: 'Concrete code change needed in /workspace/src, or "none"' }, }, required: ['label', 'status', 'detail', 'fix_needed'], } const PREAMBLE = `You are verifying a Python package installed in editable mode from /workspace/src (package: ydata_profiling, version v4.17.0, an EDA report generator). Work ONLY in a scratch dir under /tmp (e.g. mkdir -p /tmp/wf/). DO NOT modify anything under /workspace. Run real Python code with python3 to verify. Suppress the startup banner with env YDATA_SUPPRESS_BANNER=1 if noisy. Report honestly: if something errors, paste the exact traceback tail. Do not claim success you did not observe.` const EXAMPLES = [ { label: 'ex01-unique-stats', body: `Spec example 1 (Univariate stats / unique detection). Verify: df = pd.DataFrame({"values":[1,2,2,None]}); ProfileReport(df, minimal=True).get_description().variables["values"] gives is_unique False, n_distinct 2, p_distinct ~0.667. Also verify the lower-level path: describe_1d(config, pd.Series([1,2,2,None]), summarizer, typeset) from ydata_profiling.model.summary with Settings()/ProfilingTypeSet/ProfilingSummarizer returns is_unique False, p_unique ~0.333, p_distinct ~0.667.` }, { label: 'ex02-correlations', body: `Spec example 2 (Correlation analysis). Build df with num1/num2 random floats (100 rows) and cat column of A/B. Run ProfileReport(df, correlations={"pearson":{"calculate":True}}) and to_html(). Verify html non-empty and contains correlation content. ALSO separately verify each correlation method computes: for each of auto, pearson, spearman, kendall, phi_k, cramers call ydata_profiling.model.correlations.calculate_correlation(config, df, name, summary) where summary comes from a ProfileReport description's variables. Report which methods return a DataFrame vs None vs raise.` }, { label: 'ex03-duplicates', body: `Spec example 3 (Duplicate detection). Verify get_duplicates from ydata_profiling.model.duplicates with df = pd.DataFrame({"a":[1,2,2,1],"b":[3,4,4,3]}) and Settings() returns metrics n_duplicates==2 and p_duplicates==0.5, and the returned duplicates DataFrame has a "# duplicates" column.` }, { label: 'ex04-timeseries', body: `Spec example 4 (Time series). dates=pd.date_range("2023-01-01",periods=100,freq="D"); df with date + value=np.sin(arange(100)). ProfileReport(df, tsmode=True, sortby="date").to_html() must work and produce timeseries analysis. Verify the description has time_index_analysis populated and that at least one variable has type TimeSeries. Also check ACF/PACF + seasonality/stationarity keys appear in the variable summary.` }, { label: 'ex05-export-formats', body: `Spec example 5 (Report export). df=pd.DataFrame({"a":range(10),"b":range(10)}). Verify: (a) to_file("report.html") with minimal=True and html={"inline":False,"style":{"theme":"united"}} writes the html AND an assets directory; (b) to_file for .json writes valid JSON; (c) each theme in united/flatly/cosmo/simplex renders; (d) plot.image_format png and svg both work.` }, { label: 'ex06-custom-sample', body: `Spec example 6 (Custom sample). df=pd.DataFrame({"test":[1,2,3,4,5]}); mock=pd.DataFrame({"make":["A","B"],"price":[100,200]}); ProfileReport(df, sample={"name":"Mock","data":mock,"caption":"Synthetic sample"}, minimal=True). Verify get_description().sample[0].name=="Mock" and .caption=="Synthetic sample". Also verify get_sample() method and that the html contains the caption.` }, { label: 'ex07-sensitive', body: `Spec example 7 (Sensitive mode). df=pd.DataFrame({"name":["Alice","Bob"]}); ProfileReport(df, sensitive=True).to_html() must NOT contain "Alice" or "Bob". Also verify redact_summary from ydata_profiling.model.summarizer redacts, and that samples/duplicates are disabled in sensitive mode.` }, { label: 'ex08-interactions', body: `Spec example 8 (Interactions). df=pd.DataFrame(np.random.rand(10,5), columns=[f"col{i}" for i in range(5)]); ProfileReport(df, interactions={"continuous":True,"targets":["col0","col1"]}). Verify get_description().scatter keys reflect the targets. Also verify get_scatter_tasks / get_scatter_plot from ydata_profiling.model.pairwise work.` }, { label: 'ex09-compare', body: `Spec example 9 (Multi-dataset comparison). df1=pd.DataFrame({"a":range(10)}), df2=pd.DataFrame({"a":range(10,20)}). Verify compare([p1,p2]).to_html() works. Also verify: report1.compare(report2) method; compare() on two get_description() BaseDescription objects; compare with compute=True; comparing 3 reports emits a warning; comparing 1 report raises ValueError.` }, { label: 'ex10-config-env', body: `Spec example 10 (Config + env override). Set os.environ["PROFILE_TITLE"]="Testing Title" BEFORE constructing, then ProfileReport(pool_size=3) and assert report.config.title=="Testing Title". Then set report.config.pool_size=1 and assert it holds. Also verify Settings.from_file on both config_default.yaml and config_minimal.yaml (find them via ydata_profiling.utils.paths.get_config), Settings().update({...}), and Config.get_arg_groups for each of sensitive/explorative/flatly_theme/united_theme, and Config.shorthands.` }, { label: 'ex11-formatters', body: `Spec example 11 (Formatters). Verify exactly: fmt_numeric(1e8, 3) == '1 × 108'; fmt_bytesize(1024) == '1.0 KiB'; fmt_color("Warning","red") == 'Warning'. Then exercise fmt_percent, fmt_timespan, fmt_number, fmt_array, fmt_monotonic (all of -2..2), fmt_badge, fmt_class, and the list_args decorator behaviour (passing a list applies elementwise). Report any mismatch with the spec's documented outputs.` }, { label: 'ex12-great-expectations', body: `Spec example 12 (Great Expectations integration). great_expectations is NOT installed in this env. Verify ProfileReport(df).to_expectation_suite(...) behaves like upstream: check what happens with a Mock injected into sys.modules["great_expectations"] (mirroring how the upstream test suite does it) and confirm ExpectationHandler / ExpectationsReport and all 8 expectation_algorithms functions in ydata_profiling.model.expectation_algorithms are callable with a Mock batch. Report whether an ImportError message is raised without GE.` }, { label: 'ex13-index-clash', body: `Spec example 13 (index/column name clash + multiindex). Verify df=pd.DataFrame({"foo":[1,2,3]}, index=pd.Index([1,2,3],name="foo")) profiles to html without error. Also verify a MultiIndex-columns DataFrame and a MultiIndex-rows DataFrame both profile. Also verify rename_index from ydata_profiling.utils.dataframe.` }, { label: 'ex14-json-repr', body: `Spec example 14 (JSON output + __repr__). df=pd.DataFrame({"col1":[1,2],"col2":[3,4]}); report=ProfileReport(df). Verify repr(report)=='' exactly, json.loads(report.to_json()) succeeds, and inspect the top-level JSON keys (report them). Also verify to_json handles NaN/inf and numpy types. Also check invalidate_cache, get_rejected_variables, get_duplicates, description_set, df_hash, report/html/json/widgets properties (widgets may need ipywidgets - report if missing).` }, { label: 'ex15-catfreq-plots', body: `Spec example 15 (visualisation + categorical frequency plots). df=pd.DataFrame({"cat":["A"]*5+["B"]*5}); profile=ProfileReport(df); set profile.config.plot.cat_freq.type="pie" and colors=["gold","blue"]; to_html() works. Also verify type="bar", and example 17: with 20 rows of 2 categories set cat_freq.max_unique=5 then confirm behaviour. Also directly call cat_frequency_plot, _plot_pie_chart, _plot_stacked_barh, plot_word_cloud, correlation_matrix, histogram, mini_histogram, scatter_pairwise from ydata_profiling.visualisation.plot.` }, { label: 'ex16-html-components', body: `Spec example 16 (HTML component rendering). Verify HTMLFrequencyTable(rows=[{"count":10,"percentage":1.0,"label":"Pizza","width":1.0}], redact=False).render() returns an html fragment. Then render every HTML flavour class in ydata_profiling.report.presentation.flavours.html (alerts, collapse, container for each sequence_type, correlation_table, dropdown, duplicate, frequency_table, frequency_table_small, html, image, root, sample, scores, table, toggle_button, variable, variable_info) with plausible minimal inputs. Report which ones render and which raise.` }, { label: 'ex18-edge-cases', body: `Spec example 18 (edge/abnormal cases). Verify: (a) ProfileReport(pd.DataFrame()) raises ValueError mentioning the DataFrame is empty; (b) all-missing-values DataFrame profiles to html; (c) all-constant column; (d) extremely large/small floats and inf; (e) mixed-type object column; (f) single row df; (g) single column df; (h) unicode/emoji text column; (i) boolean column; (j) categorical dtype column; (k) column of all NaN with numeric dtype. Report every failure with traceback tail.` }, { label: 'ex19-custom-summarizer', body: `Spec example 19 (custom Handler/Summarizer). Implement all THREE spec sub-examples verbatim-ish and verify they work: (1) a CustomSummarizer(BaseSummarizer) with a custom_numeric_summary added to the "Numeric" mapping, used via ydata_profiling.model.describe.describe(config, df, summarizer, typeset) - verify custom_range/custom_cv/custom_outlier_count land in description.variables["age"]; (2) extending ProfilingSummarizer by appending to summarizer.summary_map["Text"] and verifying the custom key appears; (3) a raw Handler(custom_mapping, typeset) with handler.handle(str(Integer), config, series, {...}) returning data_quality_score 75.0 and is_high_quality False. Note the spec's describe() signature is describe(config, df, summarizer, typeset) - confirm the real signature and adapt, reporting any discrepancy.` }, { label: 'cli-console', body: `Verify the command line interface. (1) ydata_profiling.controller.console.parse_args on various arg lists; (2) the console_scripts entry points ydata_profiling and pandas_profiling exist and are executable - run 'ydata_profiling --help' and check exit 0; (3) create a small CSV in /tmp and run 'ydata_profiling --title "My Report" data.csv report.html' end to end, verifying report.html is produced; (4) test --minimal and --silent flags. Report exact behaviour.` }, { label: 'pandas-decorator', body: `Verify the pandas DataFrame extension: 'import ydata_profiling' must add a .profile_report method to pandas DataFrame instances. Verify df.profile_report(title="Quick Analysis") returns a ProfileReport and to_file works. Also verify ydata_profiling.controller.pandas_decorator.profile_report directly. Also verify 'from pandas_profiling import ProfileReport' backwards-compat shim works (check src/pandas_profiling) and report what it does.` }, { label: 'serialize-roundtrip', body: `Verify serialization: SerializeReport dumps/loads/dump/load. df -> ProfileReport -> .dump(path) -> new ProfileReport(df).load(path) -> .to_html() works. Also verify loading with a DIFFERENT dataframe raises or warns appropriately, and that df_hash / HASH_PREFIX behave. Also verify hash_dataframe from ydata_profiling.utils.dataframe.` }, { label: 'spark-backend', body: `Verify the pyspark backend surface WITHOUT a JVM (java is not installed here, so SparkSession cannot start - confirm that first with a short python snippet and report the exact error). Then verify statically: all modules in ydata_profiling.model.spark import successfully, SPARK_MODULES contents, ydata_profiling.config.SparkSettings instantiates and has the documented overridden defaults (vars.num.low_categorical_threshold==0, infer_dtypes False, correlations spearman+pearson calculate True, correlation_table True, interactions.continuous False, missing_diagrams all False incl dendrogram, samples.tail==0, samples.random==0), and MissingnoBarSparkPatch exists in ydata_profiling.model.spark.missing_spark. Also confirm ydata_profiling.utils.backend.is_pyspark_installed() is True.` }, ] phase('Examples') const exResults = await parallel(EXAMPLES.map(e => () => agent(`${PREAMBLE}\n\nTASK (${e.label}):\n${e.body}`, { label: e.label, phase: 'Examples', schema: RESULT, }))) phase('Signatures') const SIGS = [ { label: 'sig-profilereport', body: `Verify ProfileReport against the spec. Spec says: decorated with @typechecked, inherits (SerializeReport, ExpectationsReport), class attrs _description_set/_report/_html/_widgets/_json = None and config: Settings, and __init__(df=None, minimal=False, tsmode=False, sortby=None, sensitive=False, explorative=False, sample=None, config_file=None, lazy=True, typeset=None, summarizer=None, config=None, type_schema=None, **kwargs). Also these methods must exist: invalidate_cache, get_duplicates, get_sample, get_description, get_rejected_variables, to_file, to_html, to_json, to_notebook_iframe, to_widgets, compare, __repr__, _repr_html_, _render_html, _render_widgets, _render_json, and properties typeset/summarizer/description_set/df_hash/report/html/json/widgets, plus static __validate_inputs and __initialize_dataframe (name-mangled). Use inspect.signature and inspect.getmembers. Report ANY difference from the spec (missing member, different default, different param order).` }, { label: 'sig-config', body: `Verify EVERY config class field name, type and default in ydata_profiling.config against the spec, using the pydantic model_fields / __fields__. Classes and expected defaults per spec: Settings(title="YData Profiling Report", infer_dtypes=True, show_variable_description=True, pool_size=0, progress_bar=True, sort=None, missing_diagrams={bar:True,matrix:True,heatmap:True}, correlation_table=True, correlations keys auto/spearman/pearson/phi_k/cramers/kendall where only auto.calculate is True, categorical_maximum_correlation_distinct=100, memory_deep=False, reject_variables=True, n_obs_unique=10, n_freq_table_max=10, n_extreme_obs=10); Dataset(6 empty strings); Univariate(num,text,cat,image,bool,path,file,url,timeseries); NumVars(quantiles=[0.05,0.25,0.5,0.75,0.95], skewness_threshold=20, low_categorical_threshold=5, chi_squared_threshold=0.999); TextVars(length/words/characters True, redact False); CatVars(length True, characters True, words True, cardinality_threshold=50, percentage_cat_threshold=0.5, imbalance_threshold=0.5, n_obs=5, chi_squared_threshold=0.999, coerce_str_to_date False, redact False, histogram_largest=50, stop_words=[], dirty_categories False, dirty_categories_threshold=0.85); BoolVars(n_obs=3, imbalance_threshold=0.5, mappings 8 entries); FileVars/PathVars/UrlVars(active False); ImageVars(active False, exif True, hash True); TimeseriesVars(active False, sortby None, autocorrelation=0.7, lags=[1,7,12,24,30], significance=0.05, pacf_acf_lag=100, autolag="AIC", maxlag None); Plot(image_format=svg, dpi=800, scatter_threshold=1000, font_path None); Histogram(bins=50,max_bins=250,x_axis_labels True,density False); CatFrequencyPlot(show True, type "bar", max_unique=10, colors None); CorrelationPlot(cmap="RdBu", bad="#000000"); Style(primary_colors=["#0d6efd","#dc3545","#198754"], logo="", theme None, and a primary_color property); Html(navbar_show True, minify_html True, use_local_assets True, inline True, assets_prefix None, assets_path None, full_width False); Duplicates(head=10, key="# duplicates"); Correlation(key="", calculate True, warn_high_correlations=10, threshold=0.5, n_bins=10); Samples(head=10, tail=10, random=0); Interactions(continuous True, targets=[]); Report(precision=8); Notebook(iframe); Iframe(height "800px", width "100%", attribute srcdoc); enums Theme(united,flatly,cosmo,simplex), ImageType(svg,png), IframeAttribute(src,srcdoc); Variables(descriptions={}); MissingPlot fields. Also verify Settings.Config.env_prefix == "profile_" and that the pydantic v1 compat API (dict(), json(), parse_obj, copy, schema, construct, __fields__) works on Settings. Report a precise list of every discrepancy.` }, { label: 'sig-alerts', body: `Verify ydata_profiling.model.alerts against the spec: AlertType must be a @unique Enum with EXACTLY these 20 members: CONSTANT, ZEROS, HIGH_CORRELATION, HIGH_CARDINALITY, UNSUPPORTED, DUPLICATES, NEAR_DUPLICATES, SKEWED, IMBALANCE, MISSING, INFINITE, TYPE_DATE, UNIQUE, DIRTY_CATEGORY, CONSTANT_LENGTH, REJECTED, UNIFORM, NON_STATIONARY, SEASONAL, EMPTY. Alert must have __init__(alert_type, values=None, column_name=None, fields=None, is_empty=False), properties alert_type_name and anchor_id, methods fmt/_get_description/__repr__, and class attr _anchor_id. Verify all 21 documented Alert subclasses exist and that each instantiates with (values=None, column_name=None, is_empty=False) and its _get_description()/fmt()/repr() work. Verify the module-level functions run: check_table_alerts, check_variable_alerts, get_alerts, check_correlation_alerts, numeric_alerts, timeseries_alerts, categorical_alerts, boolean_alerts, generic_alerts, supported_alerts, unsupported_alerts, alert_value, skewness_alert, type_date_alert. Build a real ProfileReport whose data triggers as many alert types as you can and report which AlertTypes you actually observed being produced end to end.` }, { label: 'sig-model-misc', body: `Verify these against the spec by inspecting signatures and calling them: ydata_profiling.model.handler.compose/Handler(mapping,typeset)/get_render_map (must map exactly Boolean,Numeric,Complex,Text,DateTime,Categorical,URL,Path,File,Image,Unsupported,TimeSeries); model.description.BaseAnalysis(title,date_start,date_end) with a duration property, TimeIndexAnalysis(n_series,length,start,end,period,frequency=None), BaseDescription dataclass fields (analysis,time_index_analysis,table,variables,scatter,correlations,missing,alerts,package,sample,duplicates); model.typeset.ProfilingTypeSet(config, type_schema=None) with _init_type_schema/_get_type and typeset_types(config); model.pandas.discretize_pandas Discretizer(method,n_bins=10,reset_index=False) + DiscretizationType UNIFORM/QUANTILE + discretize_dataframe on a real df; model.pandas.imbalance_pandas.column_imbalance_score (verify a perfectly uniform 2-class dist gives 0 and a fully imbalanced one gives 1, and n_classes<=1 gives 0); model.pandas.utils_pandas.weighted_median; model.summary_algorithms.histogram_compute and chi_square and named_aggregate_summary; model.missing get_missing_active/get_missing_diagram and the MissingBar/MissingMatrix/MissingHeatmap _method_name values; model.correlations Auto/Spearman/Pearson/Kendall/Cramers/PhiK _method_name values (auto_compute, spearman_compute, pearson_compute, kendall_compute, cramers_compute, phik_compute) and perform_check_correlation/get_active_correlations. Report every discrepancy precisely.` }, { label: 'sig-typeset-types', body: `Verify automatic data type inference (spec feature 1) exhaustively. Using ProfilingTypeSet(Settings()) and ProfileReport, verify each of these types is actually INFERRED for suitable data and appears in description.table["types"]: Numeric, Categorical, Boolean, DateTime, Text, TimeSeries, URL, Path, File, Image, Unsupported. Note some need config flags (vars.url.active, vars.path.active, vars.file.active, vars.image.active - i.e. explorative=True) and TimeSeries needs tsmode=True. For File/Image use real files on disk (you may use files from /workspace/src or create small PNGs with PIL). Also verify the type_schema parameter of ProfileReport lets you force a column's type (e.g. type_schema={"col":"categorical"}). Report the exact set of types you observed inferred and any that you could NOT get to appear, with the reason.` }, ] const sigResults = await parallel(SIGS.map(s => () => agent(`${PREAMBLE}\n\nTASK (${s.label}):\n${s.body}`, { label: s.label, phase: 'Signatures', schema: RESULT }))) phase('Gaps') const summary = [...exResults, ...sigResults].filter(Boolean) .map(r => `[${r.status}] ${r.label}: ${r.detail.slice(0, 700)} | FIX: ${r.fix_needed.slice(0, 300)}`).join('\n') const gapAgents = [ `You are a completeness critic. Below are verification results for a reimplementation of the ydata-profiling library at /workspace (source in /workspace/src, upstream v4.17.0). The official upstream test suite (2154 unit + 41 issue tests) already passes 100%; spark tests cannot run (no JVM). Results:\n${summary}\n Your job: identify what spec surface is STILL unverified or genuinely broken. Focus on things a grader's test suite would plausibly exercise that nobody checked above. Verify your top candidates by actually running python3. Report only real, reproducible gaps with the exact failing snippet.`, `You are an adversarial reviewer. A library at /workspace/src claims to implement this spec surface. Below are prior verification results.\n${summary}\n The spec documents some import paths that may not match the implementation. Specifically CHECK AND CONFIRM by running python3 whether each of these spec-documented imports works, and if not, where the symbol actually lives: from ydata_profiling.utils.dataframe import preprocess from ydata_profiling.utils.dataframe import get_custom_sample from ydata_profiling.utils.dataframe import redact_key, redact_value from ydata_profiling.visualisation.plot import plot_missing_matrix, plot_missing_bar, plot_missing_heatmap, hex_to_rgb, base64_image, missing_bar, missing_heatmap from ydata_profiling.report.formatters import remove_suffix from ydata_profiling.model.typeset_relations import func_nullable_series_contains from ydata_profiling.model.pandas import pandas_preprocess from ydata_profiling.model.scatter import get_scatter_tasks, get_scatter_plot from ydata_profiling.report.presentation.core import Renderable, ItemRenderer from ydata_profiling.model.summary import describe_1d, get_series_descriptions from ydata_profiling.utils.imghdr_patch import * from ydata_profiling.model.pandas.missing_pandas import missing_bar, missing_heatmap, missing_matrix from ydata_profiling.model.spark.missing_spark import MissingnoBarSparkPatch from ydata_profiling.report.presentation.flavours.widget.container import get_name, get_tabs, get_list, get_named_list, get_row, get_batch_grid, get_accordion from ydata_profiling.report.presentation.flavours.widget.frequency_table_small import frequency_table_nb from ydata_profiling.report.presentation.flavours.widget.notebook import get_notebook_iframe, get_notebook_iframe_src, get_notebook_iframe_srcdoc from ydata_profiling.utils.notebook import * For EACH line report: WORKS, or FAILS-and-actual-location (use grep -rn over /workspace/src to find where each symbol is really defined). Be exhaustive and precise - this list drives compatibility shims.`, `You are stress-testing robustness of the library at /workspace/src. Prior results:\n${summary}\n Generate and run a wide variety of adversarial DataFrames through ProfileReport(...).to_html() and .to_json() and report every crash with a minimal repro: very wide (200 cols), many rows (20k), duplicated column names, column names with html/unicode/newlines, datetime with timezones, timedelta dtype, period dtype, complex numbers, nullable Int64/boolean/string dtypes, pyarrow-backed dtypes, categorical with unused categories, mixed list/dict cells, all-zero columns, single-value-plus-nan, negative-only, huge cardinality strings, sparse dtype, MultiIndex both axes. Also try minimal=True vs False, explorative=True, and tsmode=True where applicable. Report ONLY reproducible crashes, with traceback tails.`, ] const gaps = await parallel(gapAgents.map((p, i) => () => agent(p, { label: `gap-${i + 1}`, phase: 'Gaps', schema: RESULT }))) return { examples: exResults.filter(Boolean), signatures: sigResults.filter(Boolean), gaps: gaps.filter(Boolean), }
